_readme: Day-one CLOSED-WORLD allow-list for the E2E wire journal (backlog Workstream C, items C3/C4).
Consumed by tooling/e2e/ci/check-wire-journal.sh. ANYTHING ABSENT FROM `kinds` IS FORBIDDEN —
that is the whole point, and it is what makes this stronger than the forbid-list it replaces
(_assertWirePrivacyInvariants in haven/integration_test/e2e/e2e_combined.dart, which enumerated
{3, 443, 10051} and let every other new kind through in silence).
Two directions are asserted per entry, never set equality:
observed tags MUST be a SUBSET of `tags.allowed`   — catches anything NEW reaching a relay;
`tags.required` MUST be a SUBSET of observed tags  — catches a feature that silently STOPPED.
`required` at the kind level is the same superset check one level up.
Both checks are evaluated over the UNION of a kind's de-duplicated events, not per event.
That is deliberate: a kind-445 commit carries `h` alone while an application message also
carries `expiration`, so a per-event required-set would false-red on every commit. The
per-event tag-set discrimination for kind 445 is backlog item C5.3 and lives elsewhere.
SEND-SIDE. Both directions are evaluated over CLIENT->RELAY events only. The journal records
`dir`, so the oracle knows more than a relay does, and spending that knowledge is what makes
the entries below assertions about HAVEN rather than about whoever happened to be on the
wire. Two shapes forced it: a run publishing only 30443 satisfied `required` for 445 and 1059
from INBOUND copies, and a run in which every 445 Haven sent had lost its `expiration`
reported clean because one inbound 445 still carried it. The inbound kind set is printed as
an advisory and never asserted; inbound tag/kind facts belong to check-wire-correlation.sh.
Every entry below was derived by reading the construction sites, not from the protocol table
in CLAUDE.md. Where the two disagreed, the code won; the disagreements are recorded in `_why`.
This file is LINTED by its consumer on every run (and standalone via `--lint-allowlist`):
shape, `tags.required` subset of `tags.allowed`, `frame_verbs.required` subset of
`frame_verbs.allowed`, and — the invariant the whole closed-world argument rests on — that no
kind appears in both `kinds` and `_forbidden_by_omission`.

_why: AUTH (NIP-42) and COUNT (NIP-45) are deliberately EXCLUDED even though the journal
contract lists AUTH among the frames the recorder recognises. Recognised is not expected:
neither hermetic relay is configured for auth (tooling/e2e/strfry.conf:3 'no auth';
tooling/e2e/local-relay/src/main.rs is a bare RelayBuilder with none), and Haven has no
NIP-42 client support at all. An AUTH frame on this wire therefore means something changed
and is worth a human look — which is exactly the verdict a closed set should produce.
HAVEN_WIRE_SENTINEL is the recorder's own snapshot marker (SENTINEL_VERB in
tooling/e2e/local-relay/src/frame.rs). The proxy intercepts it and never forwards it, so
no relay ever sees it — but it IS journalled as a c2r frame, so a closed verb set has to
admit it. It is also REQUIRED: a journal with no marker cannot be anchored, and having the
verb set say so keeps that fact visible in the same place the rest of the closed world is
declared, rather than only inside the script.
A REQ is the other thing a client puts on a relay, and the structural oracle used to reduce
it to its verb — so a filter carrying `authors`, `#p`, `#h`, `search` or `#g` was clean
while the run summary printed `verbs [... REQ ...]` as if the frame had been read. These are
KEY names only; the VALUES (how many authors, how many `#h`, whether two relay sets were
merged) are check-wire-correlation.sh's C5.2 and are deliberately not duplicated here.
Derived from the construction sites, same rule as `kinds`:
kinds   <- Filter::kind/kinds, ~21 sites incl. haven-core/src/relay/live_sync/planes/
group.rs:29 and every Dart harness filter map
limit   <- Filter::limit, ~17 sites
authors <- Filter::author (NOT Filter::pubkey; see CLAUDE.md), e.g. profile fetch
#p      <- Filter::pubkey, e.g. haven-core/src/relay/live_sync/planes/inbox.rs (the
user's OWN pubkey) and the harness gift-wrap filter
#h      <- Filter::custom_tag(s)(Alphabet::H) at planes/group.rs:30 and
haven/rust_builder/src/api.rs:8007
since   <- Filter::since at planes/group.rs:34 and api.rs:8014
ids     <- the harness only (haven/integration_test/b8_clock_skew_test.dart:1048); no
Rust Filter sets it. Kept because the harness reaches the proxy on the same
loopback as the app and its REQs land in the same journal.
NOT admitted, and each absence is a real assertion: `search` (NIP-50 puts plaintext query
terms on the wire), `#g` (a geohash filter tells the relay which area the user watches),
`#t`, `#a`, `#d`, `#e`, `until`. None has a construction site in this repo.
DISAGREEMENT with check-wire-correlation.sh, recorded rather than silently reconciled: its
C5.2 key set additionally admits `until`, `#a`, `#d` and `#e`. Nothing in the repo
constructs any of the four, so this file takes the narrower code-derived set — a
closed-world list should be the smallest one the code justifies, and a false red here says
'add it WITH a rationale', which is the outcome that gets a human to look.
Zero tags: EventBuilder::metadata emits none, and the publisher deliberately adds no
client/app tag. An empty `allowed` is therefore a real assertion, not a placeholder — a
`client` tag appearing here would be a new, permanent, identity-signed public fingerprint.
NOT required: the E2E harness pre-seeds identity and skips onboarding
(TestUser.preSeedIdentityAndSkipOnboarding), so a run can legitimately publish no kind-0.
This is what the backlog means by '0/5 allowed-but-not-required'.
Two shapes: {e,a} for a replaceable-coordinate deletion, and {e} ALONE for the legacy-443
retraction, which omits the coordinate on purpose (a `443:<pubkey>:` coordinate would
delete every 443 by that author — key_package.rs:586-593). Hence no required tag: either
shape is legitimate. NOT required at kind level: deletion only fires when a prior
published-event record exists, which a fresh E2E identity does not have.

445._site: mdk transport-nostr-peeler/src/peeler.rs:145-173 (published by haven-core/src/relay/auto_commit.rs:99 and the Dart publishEvent sites)
_why: `h` is unconditional; `expiration` is pushed only when the group message carries a
retention timestamp (application messages, from group component 0x8005). Requiring BOTH at
the union level is the sharpest check in this file: it fails if the NIP-40 TTL silently
stops being stamped on location events, which no subset check can see. It is safe here
precisely because the journal records what was SENT and is immune to the NIP-40 eviction
that makes the relay-query oracle degrade. A lane that shares no location must supply its
own allow-list rather than weakening this one.
`allowed` also pins the tripwire on haven-core/src/nostr/event.rs:203-227 — a live-but-
unreachable 445 builder that stamps `alt` and a truncated 5-char geohash `g`. If it ever
becomes reachable, both tags land here as violations.
`ephemeral_pubkey` marks this kind's author as a FRESH keypair per message (Security Rule
2, mdk transport-nostr-peeler). It excludes 445s from --min-distinct-publishers, which
otherwise counted one device sending four location events as six publishers — a
'participant floor' any single client could satisfy alone.

1059._site: mdk transport-nostr-peeler/src/peeler.rs:367 (gift_wrap with empty extra-tags); published from haven/lib/src/services/nostr_circle_service.dart:581,1180
_why: Production gift wraps carry `p` and nothing else. The orphaned-but-still-pub
haven-core/src/nostr/giftwrap.rs:123-131 wrap_welcome stamps an additional 30-day
`expiration`; excluding it here means that builder becoming reachable is a violation.
`ephemeral_pubkey`: a gift wrap is signed by a throwaway key by construction (NIP-59), so
its author can never be evidence that a distinct PARTICIPANT transmitted. See kind 445.
`r` (NIP-65), never the singular `relay` used by 10050 — mixing them up is the shape of a
real bug, so the two entries are deliberately asymmetric. `r` is conditional on a non-empty
URL list: the unpublish tombstone is a zero-tag replaceable event, so `r` cannot be
required without false-redding an unpublish. See _followups for the kind-level `required`.

10050._why: Singular `relay` (NIP-17 inbox), not `r`. Same zero-tag tombstone caveat as 10002.

_why: All seven are unconditional in Haven's own builder, so all seven are required — this is a
kind Haven constructs itself rather than inheriting from MDK, which makes the strict form
safe. Note there is NO `relays` and NO `encoding` tag: an earlier draft of this file
assumed both, and the code says otherwise.

_forbidden_by_omission.3: Contact list. Constructed nowhere in the repo. Would walk the user's social graph out. Was on the old forbid-list; stays forbidden here by omission.
_forbidden_by_omission.9: Inner application message (haven-core/src/nostr/mls/manager.rs:550). An UNSIGNED rumor serialized into the MLS payload — it becomes kind-445 ciphertext and must never appear as an event on the wire. The old forbid-list did not cover this.
_forbidden_by_omission.13: NIP-59 seal. Encrypted inside the 1059 content; never transmitted as an event.
_forbidden_by_omission.443: Legacy KeyPackage. Never minted — the Dark Matter cutover only DELETES 443s (via kind 5), it never publishes one. Was on the old forbid-list.
_forbidden_by_omission.444: Welcome. Gift-wrapped inside 1059 and UNSIGNED (Security Rule 3). A bare 444 on a relay is a regression, and omitting it here preserves the bare-444 check the old oracle did by hand.
_forbidden_by_omission.450: Account identity proof. Signed into MLS leaf extension 0xF2F1 and, per CLAUDE.md, never published. Confirmed against haven-core/src/nostr/mls/signer.rs:117.
_forbidden_by_omission.10051: SEE _disagreements — this is the one place this file departs from the backlog text.
_forbidden_by_omission.10063: Blossom server list. Constructed nowhere (v2 deferral); appears only in docs.
_forbidden_by_omission.24242: Blossom authorization. Base64'd into an HTTP Authorization header (haven-core/src/profile/blossom.rs:343-352) and NEVER published to a relay. A 24242 in this journal would be a serious leak, and the old forbid-list could not see it.

10051_is_forbidden_not_allowed: The backlog's C3 line says 'Kinds 0/5/10051 allowed-but-not-required'. This file FORBIDS
There is exactly one live emit path: haven-core/src/relay/maintenance/key_package.rs:643
builds an EMPTY replaceable kind-10051 (zero tags) as a retraction, published at
haven/rust_builder/src/api.rs:7666. It fires only when the probe at api.rs:7601 finds a live
10051 authored by the user on their own relays, and only once (sentinel at api.rs:7702). The
fresh-PUBLISH path is genuinely dead: RelayTypeFfi has no KeyPackage variant and
So a 10051 can appear only on an install MIGRATING from the pre-Dark-Matter wire, which no
E2E lane is — every lane starts from a fresh identity. Admitting 10051 to the allow-list
would make this oracle strictly WEAKER than the forbid-list it replaces, which already
asserts 10051 absent (e2e_combined.dart:4354). A replacement that loosens a live check is a
regression, so the backlog line is treated as stale w.r.t. the Dark Matter migration.
If a migration lane is ever added, it should pass its own --allowlist with 10051 -> zero tags
kind_0_tags_are_empty_not_unconstrained: CLAUDE.md's protocol table describes kind 0 as 'signed by identity key' and says nothing
about tags. The code emits NONE, so the entry pins the empty set.

real journal from the full e2e_combined lane confirms both are published in it. They are
published by the relay-list maintenance heal (haven/rust_builder/src/api.rs:7938) and on a
user relay save, but this file was written before any journal existed, and marking a kind
required on an assumption would redden the lane on its first run for a reason unrelated to
